title: Reproduction in Lower and Higher Plants
subject: Biology
subtitle: Class 12 HSC & MHT-CET / NEET • Quick Revision

nodes.title: Asexual Reproduction & Vegetative Propagation
points: Asexual reproduction: Produces genetically and morphologically identical offspring (clones). Mechanisms: Fragmentation (Spirogyra), Budding (Yeast), Spore formation (Chlamydomonas zoospores, Penicillium conidia).

Natural vegetative propagation: Roots (Sweet potato, Dahlia, Asparagus); Stems (Rhizome in Ginger/Turmeric, Tuber in Potato, Runner in Lawn grass/Cynodon, Offset in Pistia/Eichhornia); Leaves (Bryophyllum epiphyllous foliar buds, Kalanchoe).

Artificial vegetative propagation: Stem cutting (Rose, Sugarcane), Root cutting (Blackberry), Leaf cutting (Sansevieria); Grafting (Scion joined to Stock; cambium alignment mandatory; monocots cannot be grafted due to scattered closed vascular bundles); Budding (Rose).
Micropropagation (Tissue Culture): Explant grown on nutrient medium using totipotency to produce thousands of virus-free plantlets rapidly (apical shoot meristem culture).

formulas.label: Natural vegetative structures matching
formulas.expr: Ginger = Rhizome | Potato = Stem tuber (eyes) | Bryophyllum = Foliar foliar buds | Eichhornia = Offset

formulas.label: Micropropagation regeneration pathway
formulas.expr: Explant → Callus (undifferentiated mass) → Organogenesis (Auxin/Cytokinin ratio) → Plantlets

nodes.title: Microsporogenesis & Male Gametophyte Development
points: Anther anatomy: Dithecous and tetrasporangiate. Wall layers (outer to inner): 1) Epidermis (protective); 2) Endothecium (hygroscopic α-cellulose fibrous bands aiding dehiscence); 3) Middle layers (1-3 ephemeral nutritive layers); 4) Tapetum (innermost nutritive layer, polyploid/multinucleate, secretes callase, Ubisch bodies, pollenkitt).
Microsporogenesis: Diploid Microspore Mother Cell (MMC, 2n) undergoes meiosis to form a tetrahedral tetrad of 4 haploid microspores (n).

Pollen grain: Double-walled microspore. Outer Exine composed of Sporopollenin (most chemically resistant biological substance known; contains germ pores lacking sporopollenin); Inner Intine composed of cellulose and pectin.

Male gametophyte development: 1st mitotic division yields large Vegetative cell (rich food reserve) and small spindle-shaped Generative cell. Shed at 2-celled stage in ~60% angiosperms. 2nd mitotic division of generative cell yields 2 non-motile male gametes.

formulas.label: Anther wall layers order (outer to inner)
formulas.expr: Epidermis → Endothecium → Middle layers → Tapetum

formulas.label: Microsporogenesis meiotic yield
formulas.expr: 1 Microspore Mother Cell (2n) (Meiosis) → 4 Functional Microspores / Pollen grains (n)

formulas.label: Male gametophyte mitotic cell divisions
formulas.expr: 1 Microspore (n) (1st Mitosis) → Vegetative + Generative cell (2nd Mitosis) → 2 Male Gametes (n)

nodes.title: Megasporogenesis & Female Gametophyte (Embryo Sac)
points: Anatropous ovule (most common, ~82% angiosperms): Inverted ovule with micropyle lying close to funicle. Parts: Funicle (stalk), Hilum (attachment scar), Nucellus (central parenchymatous tissue), Integuments (protective coats), Micropyle (pore), Chalaza (basal region).

Megasporogenesis: Single hypodermal Megaspore Mother Cell (MMC, 2n) undergoes meiosis forming a linear tetrad of 4 megaspores (n). 3 micropylar megaspores degenerate; 1 chalazal megaspore remains functional (Monosporic development).
Polygonum type Embryo Sac: Functional megaspore undergoes 3 successive free-nuclear mitotic divisions to produce 8 nuclei, organized into a 7-celled, 8-nucleate female gametophyte.

Embryo sac architecture: 1) Egg apparatus (micropylar end): 1 Egg cell + 2 Synergids with filiform apparatus (guides pollen tube chemotropically); 2) Antipodal cells (chalazal end, 3 cells); 3) Central cell: Largest cell containing 2 Polar nuclei that fuse into secondary diploid nucleus (2n).

formulas.label: Megasporogenesis meiotic yield
formulas.expr: 1 MMC (2n) (Meiosis) → Linear tetrad of 4 megaspores → 1 Functional Megaspore (chalazal) + 3 Degenerate

formulas.label: Polygonum embryo sac cellular organization
formulas.expr: 7-celled, 8-nucleate (3 Antipodals + 1 Central cell [2 polar nuclei] + 2 Synergids + 1 Egg cell)

formulas.label: Filiform apparatus function
formulas.expr: Finger-like projections on synergids that guide pollen tube entry via chemotropic attraction

nodes.title: Pollination Mechanisms & Outbreeding Devices
points: Pollination types: Autogamy (same flower), Geitonogamy (different flower of same plant; functionally cross-pollination, genetically self-pollination), Xenogamy / Allogamy (cross-pollination between genetically distinct plants).
Abiotic agents: Anemophily (wind: light, non-sticky pollen, feathery stigma, corn, grasses); Hydrophily (water: Epihydrophily on surface in Vallisneria; Hypohydrophily submerged in Zostera).

Biotic agents: Entomophily (insects: bright, scented, nectar-rich, sticky pollen with pollenkitt, Salvia turnpipe lever mechanism); Ornithophily (birds: bright, non-scented, copious nectar, Bignonia, Bombax); Chiropterophily (bats: nocturnal, strong scent, Anthocephalus).

Outbreeding devices: Unisexuality/Dicliny (Papaya dioecious, Maize monoecious); Dichogamy (Protandry in Sunflower, Protogyny in Gloriosa); Prepotency (Apple); Heterostyly (Primula); Herkogamy (mechanical barrier, Calotropis); Self-incompatibility (genetic block, Tobacco).

formulas.label: Pollination categories comparison
formulas.expr: Autogamy (same flower) | Geitonogamy (same plant, different flower) | Xenogamy (different plant)

formulas.label: Dichogamy types mnemonic
formulas.expr: Protandry: Androecium first (Sunflower) | Protogyny: Gynoecium first (Gloriosa)

nodes.title: Pollen-Pistil Interaction & Double Fertilization
points: Pollen-Pistil interaction: Dynamic chemical dialogue between pollen and stigma surface proteins; determines acceptance of compatible pollen and rejection of incompatible pollen.
Pollen tube entry routes: Porogamy (through micropyle - most common); Chalazogamy (through chalaza, Casuarina); Mesogamy (through integuments, Cucurbita).
Double Fertilization (discovered by S.G. Nawaschin in Lilium and Fritillaria): Unique hallmark of angiosperms consisting of two simultaneous nuclear fusions:
1. Syngamy (First fertilization): 1st male gamete (n) fuses with Egg cell (n) → Diploid Zygote (2n), developing into the embryo.
2. Triple Fusion (Second fertilization): 2nd male gamete (n) fuses with Secondary diploid nucleus (2n) → Triploid Primary Endosperm Nucleus (PEN, 3n), developing into nutritive endosperm.
Significance: Ensures nutritive tissue (endosperm) is formed only if fertilization is successful, preventing waste of maternal energy.

formulas.label: Syngamy equation
formulas.expr: Male Gamete₁ (n) + Egg Cell (n) → Zygote (2n) → Embryo

formulas.label: Triple Fusion equation
formulas.expr: Male Gamete₂ (n) + Secondary Nucleus (2n) → Primary Endosperm Nucleus (PEN, 3n)

formulas.label: Pollen tube entry routes
formulas.expr: Porogamy (via Micropyle) | Chalazogamy (via Chalaza) | Mesogamy (via Integuments)

nodes.title: Development of Endosperm & Embryo
points: Endosperm types: 1) Nuclear (~56% angiosperms): Repeated free-nuclear divisions of PEN without immediate cytokinesis (e.g. coconut water is free-nuclear endosperm; white kernel is cellular endosperm); 2) Cellular: Every division followed by wall formation (Balsam, Datura); 3) Helobial: 1st division forms two chambers, subsequent divisions free-nuclear (Asphodelus).
Angiosperm vs Gymnosperm endosperm: Angiosperm endosperm is triploid (3n, post-fertilization); Gymnosperm endosperm is haploid (n, pre-fertilization female gametophyte).
Embryogeny: Zygote divides into basal suspensor cell and terminal embryonal cell; passes through proembryo → globular → heart-shaped → torpedo → mature embryo.

Dicot vs Monocot embryo: Dicot embryo (Capsella) has 2 cotyledons and embryonal axis (epicotyl terminates in plumule, hypocotyl in radicle); Monocot embryo (Maize) has 1 shield-shaped cotyledon (Scutellum), Coleoptile (sheath protecting plumule), and Coleorhiza (sheath protecting radicle).

formulas.label: Endosperm ploidy comparison
formulas.expr: Angiosperm Endosperm = Triploid (3n, post-fertilization) | Gymnosperm Endosperm = Haploid (n, pre-fertilization)

formulas.label: Monocot embryo protective sheaths
formulas.expr: Coleoptile = Protects Plumule | Coleorhiza = Protects Radicle

nodes.title: Seed & Fruit Development: Endospermic vs Non-Endospermic
points: Seed structure: Seed coat (outer Testa and inner Tegmen derived from integuments), Cotyledon(s), and Embryonal axis. Perisperm: Persistent nucellus in mature seed (e.g. Black pepper, Beet).
Endospermic (Albuminous) seeds: Retain endosperm at maturity because it is not completely consumed during embryogeny (Castor, Maize, Wheat, Sunflower).
Non-endospermic (Exalbuminous) seeds: Endosperm completely consumed by developing embryo before seed maturation; food stored in cotyledons (Pea, Bean, Gram, Groundnut).
Fruit development: Ripened ovary. True fruit develops from ovary alone (Mango, Tomato); False fruit (Pseudocarp) incorporates floral parts like thalamus (Apple, Pear, Strawberry).
Parthenocarpy: Development of fruit without fertilization, producing seedless fruits (Banana, Pineapple; artificially induced by auxins/gibberellins).

formulas.label: Floral to seed/fruit transformation key
formulas.expr: Ovary → Fruit | Ovule → Seed | Integuments → Seed coat (Testa/Tegmen) | Nucellus → Perisperm

formulas.label: Seed classification by endosperm presence
formulas.expr: Endospermic (Albuminous): Castor, Maize | Non-endospermic (Exalbuminous): Pea, Gram, Bean

nodes.title: Apomixis, Parthenocarpy & Polyembryony
points: Apomixis: Formation of seeds without fertilization (asexual reproduction that mimics sexual reproduction).

Types of Apomixis: 1) Recurrent apomixis: Embryo sac develops from archesporial cell or diploid nucellar cell without meiosis (diploid apomixis); 2) Non-recurrent apomixis: Megaspore develops without meiosis, haploid embryo develops without fertilization (haploid parthenogenesis); 3) Adventive embryony: Embryos arise directly from diploid maternal sporophytic tissues (nucellus or integuments) e.g. Citrus, Mango.
Polyembryony (discovered by Antoni van Leeuwenhoek in Citrus): Presence of more than one embryo in a single seed (cleavage polyembryony or adventive polyembryony).

Agricultural value of apomictic seeds: Hybrid vigor (heterosis) can be maintained indefinitely across generations without segregation of hybrid characters, saving farmers from purchasing costly hybrid seeds every year.

formulas.label: Apomixis definition
formulas.expr: Production of viable seeds without syngamy and meiosis (mimics sexual reproduction)

formulas.label: Polyembryony types
formulas.expr: Cleavage polyembryony (zygote splits) | Adventive polyembryony (nucellus/integument cells form embryos)

nodes.title: High-Weightage Board Diagrams & Distinctions
points: Board Diagram 1: V.S. of Anatropous Ovule (label: funicle, hilum, micropyle, nucellus, embryo sac, integuments, chalaza).
Board Diagram 2: 7-celled, 8-nucleate mature female gametophyte / Polygonum embryo sac.
Board Diagram 3: Stages of microsporogenesis and 2-celled pollen grain structure.
Board Distinguish 1: Anemophily vs Entomophily (light pollen, feathery stigma vs scented, bright petals, sticky pollenkitt).
Board Distinguish 2: Albuminous (endospermic) vs Exalbuminous (non-endospermic) seeds.
Board Distinguish 3: Double fertilization in Angiosperms vs Gymnosperms.

formulas.label: Meiotic divisions needed for N seeds formula
formulas.expr: Meiotic divisions = N + (N / 4) = 5N / 4 (e.g. for 100 seeds = 100 + 25 = 125 meiotic divisions)

formulas.label: Pollen yield from Microspore Mother Cells
formulas.expr: Number of pollen grains = 4 × Number of Microspore Mother Cells (MMC)

nodes.title: MHT-CET & NEET High-Speed Shortcuts & Traps
points: TRAP 1: Number of meiotic divisions to produce N seeds: N female gametes require N meiosis (3 degenerate) + N male gametes require N/4 meiosis. Total = N + N/4 = 1.25 N. (For 100 seeds = 125 meiosis).
TRAP 2: Endosperm ploidy: Angiosperms = 3n (triploid, post-fertilization); Gymnosperms = n (haploid, pre-fertilization female gametophyte!).

TRAP 3: Hydrophily exceptions: Not all aquatic plants are pollinated by water! Water hyacinth (Eichhornia) and Water lily (Nymphaea) are pollinated by INSECTS or WIND (flowers emerge above water level).
TRAP 4: Salvia pollination: Entomophily via 'Turn-pipe' / 'Lever mechanism' of stamens.
TRAP 5: Perisperm vs Endosperm: Perisperm is diploid (2n, persistent nucellus in black pepper, beet); Endosperm is triploid (3n).
TRAP 6: Ploidy of ovule parts: Nucellus (2n), Integuments (2n), Funicle (2n), Synergids (n), Antipodals (n), Secondary nucleus (2n), PEN (3n).

formulas.label: Meiotic divisions shortcut formula
formulas.expr: Total Meiosis for N seeds = N + ceil(N / 4) (e.g. 100 seeds → 125 meiosis; 200 seeds → 250 meiosis)

formulas.label: Aquatic plant pollination trap
formulas.expr: Eichhornia (water hyacinth) & Nymphaea (water lily) = Entomophily / Anemophily (NOT hydrophily!)

formulas.label: Ploidy quick check in angiosperm ovule
formulas.expr: Nucellus (2n) | Integuments (2n) | Synergids (n) | Antipodals (n) | PEN (3n) | Zygote (2n)
